geometry_edits.rationale: Promote the void to the dominant public-space controller so the frontage can read as an active court rather than a minor subtraction.
Widen the court carve to make the open ground figure more usable and more visible in all views.
Open the carved court toward the verified access side to match the site relation and program threshold contract.
Pull the terrace link down into a more explicit ground-level seam so the entry reads as a public undercut/connection.

graph_edits.rationale: Strengthen the program-facing void so the mass reads as a courtyard building rather than a sealed block.
Enlarge the carved public void to improve legibility of usable ground space.
Align the opening to the verified access side so the street edge becomes a public threshold.
Lower and clarify the terrace/entry connection so the ground plane reads as an inhabitable seam rather than a detached upper appendage.

rationale: The candidate reads as a coherent early massing idea in all four views: a compact rectilinear block with a stepped upper portion and one carved/offset condition. The dominant gesture is legible, and the plan does respond to the parcel without merely filling it. However, the public void/court is weakly expressed relative to the program brief, and the road frontage/access edge is not convincingly turned into an active threshold; the building reads more sealed than porous. The form is also somewhat box-like and the section does not yet strongly articulate neighborhood-living ground engagement or a clear public entry zone. It does not visibly collide across views, and repair integrity is good, but the program fit is only partial because the access-facing ground response is underdeveloped.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much more pavilion/cultural in tone; less compact neighborhood-living street-building than the brief implies.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Three-part massing around a central void with a readable bridge/threshold condition and restrained upper articulation.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Scale is more expansive and distributed than the candidate; less suited as a compact street-edge massing precedent.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Campus-like low-rise composition with a central plaza and stepped/terraced perimeter masses.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More openly commercial and horizontally spread than the current candidate; facade/transparency cues are not relevant.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Elongated low-rise mass with a carved central void and sloped/folded roof logic responding to site.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Larger and more complex than the candidate, but the terrace-ribbon principle transfers well.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced, connected low-rise wings around a central open space; section and circulation are legible as a continuous campus figure.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More fragmented and bridge-heavy than the candidate; should inform void logic, not be copied as a form.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Interlocking volumes with a substantial void and elevated connections, preserving a clear hierarchy between mass and public opening.

warnings: Verified access edge should be read as west in the program frame; the visible ground response does not clearly align with it.
The mass is coherent but too sealed for the required active street threshold.
Void logic exists but is not yet legible as usable public space.
No obvious hard-gate geometry collision is visible, but the section remains under-articulated for the program.
